answers.question: Does Cloud display the Apple system Birthdays source through EventKit and under which calendar selection/read-permission conditions?
answers.finding: Conditional device-calendar path established, not universal display. reloadCalendars takes EventKit event calendars without a birthday exclusion. Month loading requires full calendar read authorization on modern iOS and passes selected identifiers to EventKit fetching; the actual fetch likewise has no birthday-type exclusion. List row presentation explicitly recognizes EventKit birthday calendars. Thus a system Birthdays calendar and events actually exposed by EventKit can participate in this selected-calendar path.
answers.importantLimit: multiCalendarsDict explicitly excludes .birthday and .subscription, and the new-event destination resolver excludes them as writable destinations. Do not promise birthday presence in every view or editing of generated birthdays. Actual device exposure, account setup and installed release behavior were not tested.
answers.selectionUI: Other section lists otherCalendars and uses selected IDs/toggleCalendar. The grouping depends on source/local/iCloud/provider-mirror identity; do not promise a system birthday is always under a particular translated group.

answers.question: Do direct Google calendar downloads include provider birthday events or special birthday-calendar cases, and are updates one-time or recurring?
answers.finding: Generic direct-Google calendar-list/event download and all-day conversion exist. CalendarList fetch returns decoded items from one response; event pages iterate nextPageToken with a finite date window, expanded singleEvents and no eventTypes parameter. GoogleEventItem does not model eventType or birthdayProperties/contact identity. Returned events with date-only start/end are converted to ordinary all-day EventKit records.
answers.oneTimeVersusRepeated: The explicit one-time special case checks the Google holiday@group.v.calendar.google.com identifier. It is not a birthday-title test. Other mapped selected calendars can download on subsequent sync calls; a scheduled sync loop exists, but neither successful response contents nor any background/update deadline is proven. Do not call Google birthday imports one-time from the Microsoft helper: the separate Microsoft helper uses holiday/birthdays name matching.

answers.question: Does Cloud itself read/edit contact birthday fields, or must a provider/system Contacts editor be used?
answers.finding: No contact birthday-field import/edit path established. Important correction to a possible overbroad interpretation: Cloud does access Contacts in inspected source. Calendar-list Google sign-in requests calendar/contact read scopes, then calls Google connections and otherContacts import functions. These request only names,emailAddresses,phoneNumbers; Person/GoogleContact models contain no birthday. With iOS Contacts permission, the code creates/updates local names, email and phone fields using CNSaveRequest. A separate sharing picker reads contact email addresses.
answers.editorialBoundary: Do not say Cloud never reads/writes contacts or that connecting Google imports contact birthdays. For contact-derived birthdays, identify the owning provider/contact card and follow that provider’s current source-edit instructions. Apple and Google edit/delete/sync semantics must remain separately attributed. A manual yearly event is a different record.
answers.limits: No assertion of periodic contact synchronization or contact birthday preservation/deletion outcome; the actual reviewed save paths do not assign birthday fields. Source presence is not released behavior.

answers.question: Which existing widget and alert limitations apply to these all-day records without promising a birthday-specific widget or reminder?
answers.finding: Upcoming-event widget snapshots and Live Activity filter out all-day events and past/started records. This applies to an all-day birthday without requiring a special birthday rule. Event notifications differ: they can include all-day records but require actual alarms, selected calendars, enabled app notifications and allowed system authorization; scheduling has finite budgets and future-fire-date checks.
importantLimits: No birthday-specific widget, automatic birthday alarm or audible/delivery guarantee.
The direct Google event DTO does not carry reminders and the inspected new-local-event conversion creates no EKAlarm. Do not imply that Google birthday reminders accompany a mirrored all-day record.
All-day notification-body support is not proof every system birthday exposes alarms or that Apple Calendar default birthday alerts are reproduced.
An omitted widget entry is not evidence of lost calendar/contact data.
